scorer]] }} [[File:Mike James 2019 (cropped).jpg|230px|thumb|James in 2019]] '''Michael Perry James''' (born August 18, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He was a high school basketball standout playing for [[Grant High School (Portland, Oregon)|Grant High School]] in Portland, and played [[college basketball]] for [[Eastern Arizona College]] and [[Lamar Cardinals basketball|Lamar University]]. James was the first player in NBA history to go from a [[two-way contract]] to a regular contract, all while never being sent down to the [[NBA G League]] in the process. James started his professional career in Europe in 2012 and is five-time [[All-EuroLeague]] selection. He was the [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy|EuroLeague scoring champion]] in 2019. Since 2024, James is the all-time scoring leader in EuroLeague history. He was also named [[EuroLeague MVP]] of the [[2023–24 EuroLeague|2023–24 season]]. ==Early life and career== James was born and raised in [[Portland, Oregon]]. While in Portland, he played basketball for [[Grant High School (Portland, Oregon)|Grant High School]] under coach Tony Broadous.{{cite web |url=http://www.lamarcardinals.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/james_mike00.html |title=Mike James Bio |work=LamarCardinals.com |access-date=December 28, 2013}} In 2007–08, as a senior, he was ranked the No. 3 player in the state and No. 184 overall.{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/michael-james/NMChF_TsEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm |title=Michael James' High School Timeline |work=maxpreps.com |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120918015137/http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/9NPpJ9-67EC3-gwrIGhIpQ/basketball-winter-07-08/profile-michael-james.htm |archive-date=September 18, 2012 |url-status=live |access-date=December 28, 2013 }} He was also only recruited by [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] universities at the time.{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/mike-james-suns-nba-summer-league-contract-lamar-eric-bledsoe-josh-jackson-trade-news-rumors/1ne8p0uog3epe171r8r8auyu1h|title=After decade full of constant change, Mike James finally finds seat at NBA table|last=Vecenie|first=Sam|date=2017-08-11|work=Sporting News|access-date=2018-02-17}} James averaged 15 points, 4 rebounds and 3 steals per game. The team went on to win the 2008 Oregon state championship, defeating [[Oregon City High School|Oregon City]] for it. ==College career== ===Eastern Arizona College=== James started his college career at [[Eastern Arizona College]], a national junior college where he played under coach Maurice Leitzke. In his first year, he averaged 20 points per game shooting 42 percent overall, 33.3 percent from [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] range and 78 percent free throws. He was named all-conference and all-region teams as well as being ranked No. 40 best junior college player by Rivals.com. As a sophomore, he was the fourth-leading scorer in the [[NJCAA]] Division I recording 26 points per game. In addition he contributed 5 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals. ===Lamar University=== In 2010, James transferred to an NCAA Division I school, [[Lamar Cardinals basketball|Lamar University]] in [[Beaumont, Texas]] where he played under coach [[Steve Roccaforte]] in 2010–11 and coach [[Pat Knight]] in the [[2011–12 Lamar Cardinals basketball team|2011–12]] NCAA season. Playing a little over 18 minutes a game, he averaged 12.5 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.1 steals. He led the team in scoring, even though he only started two out of twenty-four games for the season. He registered a 52-point game on January 4, 2011, against [[Louisiana College]], which the Lamar Cardinals won 114–62,{{cite web |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/collegebasketball/index.ssf/2011/01/former_grant_high_standout_mik.html |title=Former Grant High standout Mike James scores 52 points for Lamar University |work=OregonLive.com |date=January 5, 2011|access-date=December 28, 2013}} breaking the previous record of 50 set by Mike Oliver in 1980.{{cite web |url=http://www.lamarcardinals.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/010411aab.html |title=Mike James scores 52 points to set Lamar record |work=Lamar Cardinals.com |date=January 4, 2011 |access-date=December 28, 2013}} In addition, he broke Lamar University's Montagne Center record for most points scored in a single game with 52, [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]]s made with 18, field goal attempts with 35, three-pointers made with 11, and three-point attempts with 21. In his senior season (2011–12), he averaged 17.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2 assists and 1.6 steals per game shooting 45.3 percent overall.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/2528096/mike-james |title=Mike James Stats, Bio |work=ESPN.com |access-date=April 9, 2023}} One notable game of his was against the 2012 NCAA champion [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]], in which he scored 29 points. His senior season ended in the first round of the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]] with a loss against [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont]]. By the end of his season, he was named All-[[Southland Conference|Southland]] First Team, Southland Tournament MVP and Southland Conference Player of the Week three times in four weeks. He had majored in [[Bachelor of General Studies|general studies]] during his time there.{{Cite web |last=Boone |first=Raven |date=2017-10-25 |title=After toiling overseas, Suns rookie Mike James is talk of the town |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/1289235/after-toiling-overseas-27-year-old-suns-rookie-mike-james-is-talk-of-town/ |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=Arizona Sports |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Mike James - 2011-12 - Men's Basketball |url=https://lamarcardinals.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/mike-james/999 |access-date=2024-02-17 |website=Lamar University Athletics |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Zagreb (2012)=== In August 2012, James signed with [[KK Zagreb|Zagreb]] of [[HT Premijer liga|Croatia]] for the 2012–13 season.{{Cite web|url=http://mlbb.d11.gr/feed-items/croatia-kk-zagreb-inks-mike-james|title=Croatia - KK Zagreb inks Mike James|date=August 24, 2012|website=mlbb.d11.gr|language=en|access-date=2018-02-17}} In December 2012, he left Zagreb. ===Hapoel Galil Elyon (2013)=== In February 2013, he signed with [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] of the [[Liga Leumit (basketball)|Israeli second-tier league]] for the rest of the season. ===Paffoni Omegna (2013–2014)=== In July 2013, James signed with Paffoni Omegna of Italy under their [[Serie B Basket|DNA Silver Basket]] league name for the 2013–14 season.{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/legadue-gold/59747/omegna-signs-mike-james.html|title=Paffoni Fulgor Omegna, ufficiale la firma di Mike James|last=Carchia|first=Emiliano|date=July 18, 2013|work=Sportando|access-date=2018-02-17|language=it}} That season, they finished in fourth place for the DNA Silver portion of the league. ===Kolossos Rodou (2014)=== In August 2014, James signed a one-year contract with [[Kolossos Rodou B.C.|Kolossos Rodou]] of [[Greek Basket League|Greece]].{{cite news|title=Mike James signs with Kolossos Rodi|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/132145/mike-james-signs-with-kolossos-rodi.html|access-date=December 18, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=August 21, 2014}} ===Baskonia (2014–2016)=== On December 2, 2014, he left Kolossos and signed with the Spanish club [[Laboral Kutxa Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Laboral Kutxa picks up scorer James|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/146419/180/laboral-kutxa-picks-up-scorer-james|access-date=December 18, 2014|work=Eurolague.net|date=December 2, 2014}} In July 2015, James joined the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Suns Announce 2015 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-announce-2015-summer-league-roster|access-date=July 22, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2015}} That same month, after a successful Summer League performance, he re-signed with Baskonia for one more season.{{cite news|title=Baskonia re-signs Mike James|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/167414/baskonia-re-signs-mike-james.html|access-date=July 22, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 6, 2015}} During that season, Saski Baskonia would reach the [[EuroLeague Final Four]], losing to the [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Ülker]] and the [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban]] for a fourth-place performance. ===Panathinaikos (2016–2017)=== On July 3, 2016, James signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] in Greece for the 2016–17 season.{{Cite news | url = http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=44089 | script-title=el:Τζέιμς ο δεύτερος | publisher = Panathinaikos B.C. | date = July 3, 2016 | access-date = July 3, 2016 | language = el}} That year saw him perform his best work in the [[EuroLeague]] yet. He helped the Panathinaikos win both the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]] title and the [[Greek Basket League]] championship in the 2016–17 season. He was later named the [[Greek Basket League Most Spectacular Player|Greek Basket League's Most Spectacular Player]] that year as well. ===Phoenix Suns (2017)=== On July 3, 2017, James signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] and joined the team for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |last=Gautier |first=Tony |date=July 3, 2017 |title=Suns Sign Mike James |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-mike-james-0 |access-date=2023-04-09 |work=NBA.com}} In the 2017 Summer League, he led the team in points and assists, averaging 20.5 points off of 53.8% shooting and 5.0 assists per game, as well as recording 5.2 rebounds and 1.8 steals in 33.2 minutes per game for the six games the Suns played during the event. James's contract with the team was a two-way affiliate deal, their first in franchise history. He also became the first player to sign a [[two-way contract]] in the NBA after spending multiple years overseas in international leagues. While James was eligible to split his time between Phoenix and their [[Northern Arizona Suns]] [[G League]] affiliate, he never joined the G League team during his two-way contract. James made his NBA debut on October 18, 2017, against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], recording 12 points that night.{{Cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/10/18/phoenix-suns-suffer-worst-loss-franchise-history-season-opening-loss-portland-trail-blazers/778981001/|title=Phoenix Suns suffer worst loss in franchise history in season-opening loss to Portland Trail Blazers|last=Bordow|first=Scott|date=October 18, 2017|work=azcentral|access-date=2018-02-17|language=en}} James became the first player to sign a two-way contract to also start with the team that signed him on, as he became the starting [[point guard]] on the October 23 game against the [[Sacramento Kings]] under interim head coach [[Jay Triano]], recording 18 points and a team-high 7 assists in a 117–115 win.{{Cite news|url=http://arizonasports.com/story/1288135/suns-mike-james-thrives-starting-lineup-place-eric-bledsoe/|title=Suns' Mike James thrives in first career start in place of Eric Bledsoe|last=Olson|first=Kellan|date=2017-10-23|work=Arizona Sports|access-date=2018-02-17|language=en-US}} During his first four games of the season, James recorded at least 10 or more points with increased minute production in each game.{{Cite news|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2017/10/24/16532806/mike-james-phoenix-suns-game-winner-sacramento-kings|title=The NBA just had their "welcome to Mike James" moment|last=King|first=Dave|date=October 24, 2017|work=Bright Side Of The Sun|access-date=2018-02-17}} On Halloween night, James recorded his first 20-point game with 24 points scored and four steals recorded in a 122–114 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.apnews.com/9c8172e6e4a442dd956e275caacca851/Booker-scores-32,-Suns-rally-late-to-beat-Nets-122-114|title=Booker scores 32, Suns rally late to beat Nets 122-114|last=Torres|first=Adry|date=November 1, 2017|work=AP News|access-date=2018-02-17|language=en-US}} On November 26, 2017, he scored a career-high 26 points in a 119–108 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite news |last=Cunningham |first=Cody |date=November 26, 2017 |title=Mike James Scores Career High Against Timberwolves |language=en |work=Phoenix Suns |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/postgame/mike-james-scores-career-high-against-timberwolves |access-date=2023-04-09}} James would play his last game under his original two-way contract on December 5 against the [[Toronto Raptors]], recording 10 points in a 126–113 loss. During this time, James would be considered the biggest success story to date revolving around the NBA's newest implemented system.{{Cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/suns-mike-james-two-way-185001945.html|title=Suns' Mike James a two-way trailblazer|last=Feldman|first=Dan|date=December 4, 2017|work=Yahoo! Sports|access-date=2018-02-17|language=en-US}} On December 7, 2017, James's contract with the Suns was converted to a one-year regular season deal, after Phoenix waived [[Derrick Jones Jr.]]{{cite web |last=York |first=Ben |date=December 7, 2017 |title=Suns Sign Mike James to Standard NBA Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-sign-mike-james-standard-nba-contract |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=NBA.com}} However, on December 23, 2017, over two weeks after signing his one-year deal, James was waived by the Suns.{{cite news |last=Cunningham |first=Cody |date=December 23, 2017 |title=Phoenix Suns Waive Mike James |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-waive-mike-james |access-date=2023-04-09}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2018)=== On January 14, 2018, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] signed James to a new [[two-way contract]].{{cite news |date=January 14, 2018 |title=Pelicans sign Mike James to a two-way contract |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-mike-james-two-way-contract |access-date=2023-04-09}} Much like his tenure with Phoenix, James was never assigned to the NBA G League during his two-way contract with New Orleans. On February 10, 2018, he was waived by the Pelicans after appearing in four games.{{Cite news |last=Gonzalez |first=Caroline |date=February 10, 2018 |title=New Orleans Pelicans waive Mike James, Rashad Vaughn |language=en |work=New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/new-orleans-pelicans-waive-mike-james-rashad-vaughn |access-date=2023-04-09}} ===Return to Panathinaikos=== On February 13, 2018, Panathinaikos announced the return of James. He started the season playing [[shooting guard]] for the Greens, alongside [[Nick Calathes]]. On March 22, James scored the game-winning shot with 5.8 seconds left against [[Maccabi Tel Aviv]]. He finished the game with 27 points.{{cite news|title=Welcome back, Mike|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=44891&lang=2|access-date=February 13, 2018|work=paobc.gr|date=February 13, 2018}} ===Olimpia Milano (2018–2019)=== On July 13, 2018, [[Olimpia Milano]] signed James to a multi-year contract.{{cite news|title=AX Milan adds playmaker James|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8vbjpgg5plk5rb5r/ax-milan-adds-playmaker-james|access-date=July 13, 2018|work=[[EuroLeague]].net|date=July 13, 2018}} Over 30 games of the [[2018–19 EuroLeague]] season, he averaged league-high 19.8 points, along with 6.8 assists and 3.8 rebounds per game. He won the [[Alphonso Ford Trophy]], given to the top scorer of the EuroLeague.{{cite news |title=Alphonso Ford Top Scorer: Mike James, Milan |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9na65cwgf46e3tem/alphonso-ford-top-scorer-mike-james-milan |access-date=26 May 2019 |work=euroleague.net |date=6 May 2019}} But despite the statistically excellent season, the incoming Olimpia Milano coach, [[Ettore Messina]], declared Mike James wouldn't be part of the [[2019–20 Olimpia Milano season|2019–20]] team plans.{{cite news|title=Ettore Messina statement regarding Mike James' situation|url=https://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/ettore-messina-statement-regarding-mike-james-situation/|access-date=July 26, 2019|work=[[Olimpia Milano|olimpiamilano]].net|date=July 26, 2019}} James and the Italian team eventually reached an agreement and mutually parted ways on July 29, 2019. ===CSKA Moscow (2019–2021)=== On August 5, 2019, James signed a one-year contract with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-announces-mike-james/|title=CSKA Moscow announces Mike James|date=August 12, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 12, 2019}} On June 1, 2020, he signed a three-year contract extension with CSKA.{{cite news |title=CSKA officially signs Mike James to a three-year contract extension |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-officially-signs-mike-james-to-a-three-year-contract-extension/ |access-date=30 April 2021 |work=Sportando}} On April 21, 2021, he and CSKA came to an agreement that allowed the player to become a free agent until the end of the 2020–21 season. James averaged 19.3 points and 5.7 assists per game in the [[2020–21 EuroLeague]] season.{{cite news |title=CSKA Moscow announces that Mike James will sign with an NBA team for this season |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-announces-that-mike-james-is-free-to-sign-with-an-nba-team-for-this-season/ |access-date=30 April 2021 |work=Sportando}} On September 11, 2021, James and the Russian club officially reached a buy-out agreement in order to terminate their mutual contract.{{cite news|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=CSKA Moscow, Mike James part ways|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cska-moscow-mike-james-part-ways/|newspaper=Sportando|date=September 11, 2021|access-date=September 11, 2021}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2021)=== On April 23, 2021, James signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/04/23/brooklyn-nets-sign-mike-james-10-day-contract|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Mike James to 10-day Contract|date=April 23, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 23, 2021}} On the same day of his signing, James debuted for the Nets against the [[Boston Celtics]], logging eight points on 3-of-8 shooting from the field and 1-of-1 from three-point range to go along with two rebounds and two assists across 21 minutes in a 109–104 win.{{Cite web |last=Dowd |first=Tom |date=April 23, 2021 |title=Nets Notes: Mike James Debuts for Brooklyn |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/feature/2021/04/23/nets-notes-mike-james-debuts-for-brooklyn |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite web|last=Milholen|first=Chris|date=April 24, 2021|title=A look at Mike James' eventful Friday with the Nets|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2021/4/24/22400761/a-look-at-mike-james-eventful-friday-with-the-nets|access-date=April 28, 2021|website=NetsDaily}} On May 3, James signed a second 10-day contract with the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Mike James to Second 10-day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/05/03/brooklyn-nets-sign-mike-james-second-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=May 3, 2021|access-date=May 3, 2021}} On May 13, James was signed for the rest of the [[2020–21 Brooklyn Nets season|2020–21 season]].{{cite web|title=Nets Notes: Mike James Signs on for the Season|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/breaking/2021/05/13/nets-notes-mike-james-signs-on-for-the-season|website=NBA.com|date=May 13, 2021|access-date=May 13, 2021}} ===Monaco (2021–2026)=== ==== 2021–22 season ==== [[File:Mike James (basketball, born 1990) 55 AS Monaco Basket EuroLeague 20241212 (11).jpg|thumb|James in a EuroLeague game with Monaco in 2024]] On September 17, 2021, James signed with [[AS Monaco Basket]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web |title=Mike James, une star sur le Rocher |url=https://asmonaco.basketball/news/show.php?ID=29213 |website=asmonaco.basketball |access-date=September 17, 2021 |language=fr-FR |date=September 17, 2021}} On July 14, 2022, James signed a two-year contract extension with Monaco.{{Cite web |title=Monaco re-signs star Mike James through 2024|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1368674/monaco-re-signs-star-mike-james-through-2024/|website=Eurohoops|date=July 14, 2022|access-date=February 29, 2024}} ==== 2022–23 season: First EuroLeague Final Four appearance ==== On March 14, 2023, Monaco temporarily suspended James for an internal violation of team rules.{{Cite web |title=Monaco suspended Mike James |url=https://basketnews.com/news-186678-monaco-suspended-mike-james.html |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=Basket News}} After this episode, he went on to lead the team to the [[2023 EuroLeague Final Four]], the first ever appearance of the club in the Final Four. He scored 17 points in Monaco's loss in semi-finals.{{cite news |last1=Antoine |first1=Lebreton |title=FINAL FOUR DE L'EUROLEAGUE MONACO ÉLIMINÉ EN DEMI-FINALE PAR L'OLYMPIAKOS (76-62) |url=https://www.eurosport.fr/basketball/euroleague/2022-2023/final-four-de-l-euroleague-monaco-elimine-en-demi-finale-par-l-olympiakos-76-62_sto9613663/story.shtml |access-date=19 December 2023 |publisher=Eurosport.fr |date=May 19, 2023 |language=fr}} On October 26, 2023, after scoring 24 points against [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], James became the fastest player in EuroLeague history to reach 4,000 career points, doing so in 248 games.{{Cite web |title=Mike James is fastest ever to reach 4,000-point barrier|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/mike-james-is-fastest-ever-to-reach-4000-euroleague-points/|website=EuroLeague|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=February 29, 2024}} ==== 2023–24 season: EuroLeague MVP and French title ==== James was named to the [[LNB All-Star Game]] in the 2023–24 season, and on December 31, led Team World to a victory over Team France. He scored 34 points and was named the All-Star Game MVP.{{Cite web |date=2023-12-31 |title=Mike James leads Team World to win, Nadir Hifi ties French All-Star record |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/proa/1605221/mike-james-leads-team-world-to-win-nadir-hifi-breaks-french-all-star-record/ |access-date=2024-02-25 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} On March 7, 2024, Mike James became the EuroLeague's all-time leading scorer during a regular season game against [[KK Crvena zvezda|Red Star Belgrade]]. He surpassed [[Vassilis Spanoulis]] after having scored 4,464 points after the game.{{Cite web |title=US point guard Mike James becomes EuroLeague's all-time leading scorer |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/us-point-guard-mike-james-becomes-euroleagues-all-time-leading-scorer/3158640 |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=www.aa.com.tr}} On May 14, James was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] for the [[2023–24 EuroLeague|2023–24 season]] after leading Monaco to a club record in wins and scoring in double-digits in all of his games.{{Cite web |date=2024-05-14 |title=2023-24 Turkish Airlines EuroLeague MVP: Mike James, AS Monaco {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/2023-24-turkish-airlines-euroleague-mvp-mike-james-as-monaco/ |access-date=2024-05-15 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} He averaged 17.9 points, a career-high 4.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game. Monaco just failed to reach the playoffs, losing in five games to Fenerbahce in the quarterfinals, losing a crucial Game 5 at home.{{Cite web |date=2024-05-08 |title=Fenerbahçe makes history by winning Game 5 at Monaco, 79-80 {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-makes-history-by-winning-game-5-at-monaco-79-80/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} On June 14, 2024, James officially signed a lucrative three-year extension that would keep him in Monaco through 2027.{{cite news |title=Mike James prolonge à Monaco ! |url=https://asmonaco.basketball/news/show.php?ID=57438 |access-date=20 June 2024 |publisher=AS Monaco Basket |date=14 June 2024}}{{cite news |title=Mike James signs long-term extension with Monaco |url=https://basketnews.com/news-207624-mike-james-signs-long-term-extension-with-monaco.html |access-date=20 June 2024 |publisher=Basketnews.com |ref=14 June 2024}} ==== 2024–25 season: EuroLeague runners-up ==== In the [[2024–25 EuroLeague]], James led Monaco to a second Final Four appearance, returning after a one-year absence. In the quarterfinal series against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], James was crucial as he scored the game-winner in the deciding Game 5.{{Cite web |title=Mike James reacts to his game-winner in Game 5 and playing Olympiacos again |url=https://basketnews.com/news-224148-mike-james-reacts-to-his-game-winner-in-game-5-and-playing-olympiacos-again.html |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}} In the surprisingly advanced to the final of the [[2025 EuroLeague Final Four|Final Four]], becoming the first French team in 32 years to reach the European final. In the semi-final against favored [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], James had 17 points, 7 rebounds, 7 assists, leading the team to a 75–65 victory.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-23 |title=Mike James leads Monaco past Olympiacos and into championship game, 68-78 {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/mike-james-leads-monaco-past-olympiacos-and-into-championship-game-68-78/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} In the final, however, Monaco lost 70–81 to [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] to finish as runners-up, despite James adding 17 points and five rebounds.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-26 |title=Fenerbahce defeat Monaco to claim second EuroLeague title |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/basketball/articles/cq85egj1l2xo |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}} During the season, James was also recognised for his historical performance in the EuroLeague, as he was named to the All-25 EuroLeague Team, composed of the best twenty-five players in league history.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-24 |title=All-25 EuroLeague team honored at 2025 Final Four {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/all-25-euroleague-team-honored-at-2025-final-four/ |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} ====2025–2026==== On November 21, 2025, James was suspended for three games after receiving two [[technical fouls]] being ejected during a French League game.{{cite web |title=Mike James suspended for three games |url=https://basketnews.com/news-235482-mike-james-suspended-lnb-games.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=24 November 2025 |language=en}} On April 18, 2026, he was ejected during a league game against [[ASVEL Basket]], once again receiving a three-game suspension.{{cite web |first=Donatas |last=Urbonas |title=Mike James facing possible three-game suspension after ejection |url=https://basketnews.com/news-246328-mike-james-facing-possible-three-game-suspension-after-ejection.html |website=basketnews.com |date=30 April 2026 |access-date=1 May 2026 Efes (2026–present)=== On July 11, 2026, James signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=AnadoluEfesSK |number=2075838789595906226 |title=Avrupa basketbolunun simge isimlerinden biri olan ve 2024 yılında EuroLeague MVP'si de seçilen Mike James ile 1+1 sezonluk sözleşme imzaladık.}} ==The Basketball Tournament== James has played for Team Maryland and Team Hines in [[The Basketball Tournament]] (TBT), an annual single-elimination winner-take-all tournament on [[ESPN]]. In two games with Team Maryland in TBT 2016, Mike James averaged 28.5 points, 4.0 assists and 6.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Mike James statistics – TBT 2016 |url=https://hosted.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/TBTA/en/competition/26489/person/1496412/statistics? |publisher=The Basketball Tournament |access-date=22 May 2021}} James's most impressive outing was a 35-point, seven-rebound outburst in a 104–92 loss against Team Foe.{{cite web |title=Mike James game log – TBT 2016 |url=https://hosted.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/TBTA/en/competition/26489/person/1496412/gamelog? |publisher=The Basketball Tournament |access-date=22 May 2021}} Three years later in TBT 2019, James led Team Hines to the Semifinal Round in which they lost to the Golden Eagles, 68–62.{{cite web |title=Team Hines – TBT 2019 |url=https://hosted.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/TBTA/en/competition/24475/team/115509? |publisher=The Basketball Tournament |access-date=22 May 2021}} In five games, James averaged 16.4 points and 5.4 assists per game, while shooting 36.8 percent from the field.{{cite web |title=Mike James statistics – TBT 2019 |url=https://hosted.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/TBTA/en/competition/24475/person/1496412/statistics? |publisher=The Basketball Tournament |access-date=22 May 2021}} ==Controversial comment== In early August 2022, James received media attention after making critical comments about NBA star [[Stephen Curry]]. James referred to Curry as being "one-dimensional" and negatively compared Curry to other NBA stars such as [[LeBron James]], [[Kevin Durant]], [[Joel Embiid]], [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] and [[Luka Dončić]].{{cite news|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/NBA-guard-says-Steph-Curry-not-top-five-17348902.php|title=Journeyman NBA guard says Warriors' Steph Curry is 'one-dimensional'|last1=Zafran|first1=Zach|publisher=[[The San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=August 3, 2022|access-date=August 6, 2022}} Curry himself later jokingly referred to the "one-dimensional" jab from James while talking with the media at a basketball camp he was hosting for elite high school players.{{cite news|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/warriors-steph-curry-admits-pettiness-17354799.php|title=Warriors' Steph Curry winks at 'one-dimensional' jab, admits he's pettiest man alive|last1=Young|first1=Dennis|publisher=[[The San Francisco Chronicle]]|quote="It's all bad for them," Curry responded. "As one-dimensional as I am," he added, winking and cracking himself up. "I'm petty ... I'm so petty.
